canonical.name: The Euler characteristic of a compact manifold defined by rational Betti numbers
canonical.locator: page-level (definition assembled from the AT homology interface)
canonical.support: The rational-homology definition and its agreement with the cell-count Euler characteristic are assembled from the published singular-homology, cellular-homology and CW Euler-characteristic items; no source states the rational definition as the primary one, so the definition is recorded as page-level.

canonical.name: Additivity of the Euler characteristic for relative finite cell decompositions and glueings
canonical.support: The relative cell-count additivity is Milnor's and Guillemin-Pollack's alternating-sum argument; the double and product additivity are assembled from the published Mayer-Vietoris sequence and the rank lemma, with the in-run handle chain complex supplying finiteness. No single source states the pair (M,A) and the glueing form together.

canonical.name: The zero-section/graph intersection form of the local index (bridge to DT-12)
canonical.locator: page-level (Guillemin-Pollack Exercises 6-9, restated in the library's intersection conventions)
canonical.support: Guillemin-Pollack sketch the intersection-theoretic proof of Poincare-Hopf in Exercises 6-9; the DT-12 page owns the self-intersection and Euler-class machinery, so the bridge is recorded as page-level and its orientation convention is fixed locally.

canonical.name: The boundary correction and its sharpness (outwardness is a genuine hypothesis)
canonical.locator: page-level (standard caution attached to the boundary form)
canonical.support: Milnor and Robbin-Salamon state the boundary form only for outward fields; the inward-radial computation and its parity discussion are page-level and verified explicitly.

canonical.name: The Euclidean/Nielsen realisation of an index sum by an explicit field on a cell decomposition
canonical.locator: Guillemin-Pollack Ch. 3 §7, printed pp. 148-150; Robbin-Salamon Ch. 6 §6.4.4, printed p. 151
canonical.support: The cell-count realisation of chi is already published on the CW page; this pair consumes it instead of re-minting it.

canonical.name: The converse existence theorem for nowhere-zero fields (Hopf)
canonical.locator: Guillemin-Pollack Ch. 3 §6, Exercises 10-13, printed pp. 146-148; Milnor §6 remark, printed p. 40
canonical.support: The amalgamation proof is Guillemin-Pollack's Exercises 10-13 together with the extension lemma proved here from the published based Hopf classification; Milnor records the theorem as Hopf's.

canonical.name: Derivation of Poincare-Hopf from the Lefschetz fixed-point theorem
canonical.reason: Guillemin-Pollack prove the index theorem through the Lefschetz number of a tangent family; that route belongs to the next pair (DT-14), which owns the Lefschetz number and the small-time flow comparison. This pair proves the same theorem without Lefschetz so that the later derivation is not circular.

canonical.name: The obstruction-theoretic proof that the Euler class is the only obstruction to a tangent section
canonical.locator: not read in a source for this batch; the design names obstruction theory as the alternative interface
canonical.reason: The converse existence theorem is proved here by the local cancellation/amalgamation argument, so the primary-obstruction identification of the Euler class with the tangent sphere bundle is not needed and is not scaffolded; the published obstruction-theory page remains available for a future dedicated treatment.

canonical.name: The reduced degree of a map into the 0-sphere (the n=1 convention for the local index)
canonical.locator: established convention derived from the degree/reduced-homology treatment of Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 2.1 (printed p. 134)
canonical.support: Step 3a confirmed that the index definition and the Gauss-degree lemma consume a 0-dimensional degree (signed count on S^0, equivalently the reduced degree of H_0-tilde(S^0;Z)) that neither the published library nor the Step-1 scaffold supplied. The dispatch authorizes creating the missing prerequisite on this A page; the convention is fixed locally on the oriented boundary S^0 = partial[-1,1] and its scalar normalisation is recorded once here, before its consumers in the batch order.

canonical.name: Homotopy invariance and multiplicativity of the reduced degree into the 0-sphere
canonical.locator: established convention derived from the degree/reduced-homology treatment of Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Section 2.1 (printed p. 134)
canonical.support: The two properties of the local prerequisite that the n=1 clause of the index definition and the chart-independence lemma actually use: a homotopy of maps into the discrete space S^0 is constant in the time variable, and the reduced degree is multiplicative under composition. Proved locally from the definitions (connectedness of the interval and product connectedness); registered so the pair's n=1 branch is fully supplied.
